name: Elliptical Trainer
summary: A low-impact cardiovascular exercise that drives linked pedals and handles to simulate running without foot strikes.

setup: Step carefully onto the foot pedals one foot at a time while holding the stationary handles for balance.
Stand upright with your core braced and grasp the moving handlebars with a comfortable neutral grip.
Select your program, resistance, and incline on the machine console.
steps: Push downward and forward with one leg while simultaneously pushing the opposite handlebar forward and pulling the same-side handlebar back.
Allow the pedals to guide your feet in a smooth, continuous elliptical path.
Transition seamlessly into pushing with the other leg to maintain a steady, rhythmic cadence.
Keep your heels grounded on the pedals rather than driving purely through the toes.
instructions.breathing: Breathe rhythmically in sync with your stride rate, matching breaths to foot cycles.

common_faults.fault: Excessive leaning on the console or stationary handles, reducing muscular engagement.
common_faults.correction: Maintain an upright posture and let your legs and core support your body weight.

common_faults.fault: Pedaling exclusively on the balls of the feet with elevated heels, placing undue strain on the calves and knees.
common_faults.correction: Keep your feet flat against the pedals and drive through the midfoot and heel.

common_faults.fault: Setting the resistance too low and relying entirely on machine momentum.
common_faults.correction: Increase resistance to maintain controlled, muscular pedal strokes at a steady cadence.

precautions: Wait for the pedals and levers to come to a complete stop before attempting to dismount the machine.
